It was sponsored by [[Carabao Energy Drink]] and known as the '''Carabao Cup''' for sponsorship reasons. The EFL Cup was open to all clubs participating in the [[Premier League]] and the [[English Football League]]. The winner of the competition qualified for the play-off round of the [[2025–26 UEFA Conference League]]. [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] were the defending champions, having beaten [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] in the [[2024 EFL Cup final|previous season's final]]. They were beaten in [[2025 EFL Cup final|this season's final]] by [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]], who won their first EFL Cup and a first domestic trophy since the [[1954–55 FA Cup]].{{cite news|url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/mar/16/newcastle-sink-liverpool-to-savour-taste-of-glory-after-decades-of-drought|title=Newcastle sink Liverpool to savour taste of glory after decades of drought|date=16 March 2025|publisher=The Guardian}} ==Teams== All 92 clubs in the Premier League and English Football League entered the season's EFL Cup. Access was distributed across the top 4 leagues of the [[English football league system]].
